title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
authors: Neda Nasiri, Seyed Mahdi Mastoor, Amirhosein Ahmadkhan Kordbacheh
abstract: The combinatorial design space of multilayer perovskite solar cells is vast, yet exhaustive experimental or computational screening of all possible material combinations remains impractical. Here, we integrate SCAPS-1D device simulations with machine learning to systematically explore 125 device architectures constructed from five electron transport layers (ETL), five absorbers (including lead-free double perovskites), and five hole transport layers (HTL). A representative subset of configurations is used to train a machine learning (ML) model, which predicts the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the remaining unexplored structures. Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation yields a Spearman rank correlation, demonstrating reliable ranking capability. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis reveals that the HTL band gap, absorber band gap, and ETL electron affinity are the most influential descriptors, providing physical insights into interfacial recombination and charge extraction. The machine learning model identifies several high-performance configurations that are subsequently verified by full SCAPS-1D simulations. Among them, the device FTO/TiO$_2$/Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$/NiO/Ag achieves a PCE of 28.85%, and the ML-suggested structure FTO/SnO$_2$/Cs$_2$AgInBr$_6$/NiO/Ag exhibits 28.62%, outperforming a closely related literature architecture by approximately 4% absolute. Notably, eight of the top-11 structures employ the lead-free double perovskite Cs$_2$AgInBr$_6$. This work demonstrates that a physics-based, data-driven workflow combining SCAPS-1D, ML, and SHAP can accelerate the discovery of high-efficiency, environmentally friendly perovskite solar cells while providing transparent design rules. The approach is generalizable to other multilayer optoelectronic systems.

infographic.key_insight: A hybrid SCAPS-1D + machine learning workflow can rapidly screen multilayer perovskite solar cells and identify high-efficiency, lead-free architectures without exhaustive brute-force simulation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The study provides actionable design rules for selecting ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations to improve charge extraction, reduce recombination, and accelerate device optimization.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL architectures in SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored structures.
Used Leave-One-Group-Out validation and SHAP to rank designs and identify key descriptors.
infographic.evidence_signal: The model showed reliable ranking via Spearman correlation in cross-validation, and the top predicted devices were confirmed by full SCAPS-1D simulations, including 28.85% PCE for FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag.
infographic.watch_item: The ML guidance depends on the simulated design space and validation set, so real-device performance may differ due to fabrication variability and unmodeled degradation mechanisms.
infographic.paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures

title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
authors: Francesco Lodola, Zhuangyi Zhou, Boaz Koren, Saeed Bayat, Alessandro Magon, Yucheng Hu
abstract: Among the highly efficient photovoltaic technologies, that do not rely on epitaxy, only chalcopyrites have a bandgap tunable down to 1.00 eV, the ideal for tandem applications. This is obtained with a pure CuInSe2 absorber without Ga. GaOx has been shown to be an efficient hole transport layer that prevents recombination at the metallic back contact. On the other hand, GaOx has proven detrimental, when it forms on In containing transparent back contacts in bifacial solar cells. Here, we investigate the conditions that make the GaOx layer conductive. We employ a GaOx hole transport layer that is formed through ion exchange during co-evaporation of the low band gap absorber layer. We find that no additional Cu is needed, and that Na is not necessary for a conductive GaOx. Nor did we find a systematic influence of oxygen flow during the sputtering process of the oxide layer. The GaOx layer is partly crystalline. The optimized passivating hole transport layer enables a CuInSe2 bottom solar cell, without any addition of Ag or heavy alkalis, with an active area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage VOC of 552meV

infographic.key_insight: A GaOx hole transport layer can be made conductive in 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells through ion-exchange formation during co-evaporation, enabling strong passivation and high voltage without added Cu, Na, Ag, or heavy alkalis.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact interface strategy for high-efficiency chalcopyrite bottom cells, helping push CuInSe2 toward tandem-ready performance with a certified VOC above 550 mV.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap absorber via ion exchange.
Tested whether Cu addition, Na, and sputter oxygen flow affect GaOx conductivity.
Characterized the oxide as partly crystalline and evaluated device performance in optimized solar cells.
infographic.evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV for a 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cell.
infographic.watch_item: GaOx conductivity appears sensitive to how the oxide forms on the back contact, so the process may not translate directly to all transparent or In-containing contact stacks.
infographic.paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?

title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
authors: Akash Dasgupta, Robert D. J. Oliver, Manuel Kober-Czerny, Charlie H. G. Nicholls, Xueli Cao, Yen-Hung Lin
abstract: Machine learning and computational inference, coupled with experimental data, promise to significantly accelerate our rate of learning in most scientific disciplines. In this study, we develop tools that connect microscopic observations to macroscopic device behaviour, a capability that is essential for accelerating the design of durable energy materials. To this end, we introduce a novel approach that integrates photoluminescence imaging with drift diffusion simulations to understand operation and degradation in fully fabricated perovskite solar cells. By employing Bayesian inference, we generate "inferred maps" of parameters that govern recombination processes present in devices. We track these parameter maps while the devices are aged (70 °C, full spectrum sunlight) to analyse their temporal evolution during degradation. Notably, our approach allows us to distinguish between degradation occurring at the hole or electron transporting layer interface, or within the bulk. Our analysis reveals pronounced spatially non-uniform degradation, with significant macroscopic heterogeneity observed in the optoelectronic parameter maps. We pinpoint the greatest degradation observed in specific regions to stem from the perovskite/transport layer interfaces. Finally, we demonstrate that an amino-silane molecular passivation treatment suppresses this degradation, highlighting its specific role in enhancing device stability. Our approach offers valuable insights for future device fabrication and is a clear exemplification of how advanced Bayesian inference can significantly increase the value of experimental data.

infographic.key_insight: Bayesian inference applied to photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize whether perovskite solar-cell degradation originates at the electron-transport layer, hole-transport layer, or within the bulk.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This gives device engineers a practical diagnostic tool to target the specific interfaces causing stability loss and to evaluate passivation strategies more effectively.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to measured optoelectronic behavior
Bayesian inference to generate spatial parameter maps and track them during aging
infographic.evidence_signal: The authors aged devices at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight and observed time-evolving, spatially non-uniform parameter maps that identified pronounced degradation at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
infographic.watch_item: The inferred maps depend on model assumptions and image-to-parameter identifiability, so results should be validated against independent physical measurements.
infographic.paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference

title: Artificial Intelligence for Instability in Inorganic Perovskites: From Mechanism Discovery to Engineering Strategies
authors: Xue Zhao, Chuan-Xin Cui, Zi-Hao Xu, Yuan-Long Pang, Jun-Jie Li, Jin-Wu Jiang
abstract: Three-dimensional all-inorganic halide perovskites, represented by CsPbX$_3$ (X = Cl, Br, I), have attracted broad interest in photovoltaics, photodetectors, and light-emitting devices because of their outstanding optoelectronic properties. Their practical deployment, however, remains limited by instability under thermal, chemical, optical, and electrical stress. Conventional studies have established important experimental and theoretical foundations, but they still struggle with multimodal data, coupled degradation pathways, protocol dependence, sparse statistics, and uncertainty quantification. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a practical route to address these limitations. This review summarizes recent progress in AI-assisted studies of instability in 3D CsPbX$_3$ and organizes the discussion around four linked tasks, including stability discrimination and diagnosis, microscopic mechanism analysis, consequence and reliability modeling, and engineering stability enhancement. We further discuss the main limitations of current methods, especially in data quality, protocol consistency, benchmark design, interpretability, and transferability across domains. Finally, we outline future directions for the field, including standardized data infrastructures, interpretable cross-scale models, and tighter integration of AI with automated experiments and physics-based modeling. The aim of this review is to provide a coherent and practically useful framework for researchers seeking to use AI to understand, predict, and mitigate instability in inorganic perovskites.

infographic.key_insight: AI can help decode, predict, and mitigate instability in 3D inorganic perovskites (CsPbX3) by linking degradation mechanisms to reliability and design strategies.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The review highlights how AI can accelerate more stable perovskite device development for photovoltaics, photodetectors, and light-emitting devices under thermal, chemical, optical, and electrical stress.
method: Stability discrimination and diagnosis
Microscopic mechanism analysis
Consequence/reliability modeling and engineering stability enhancement
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract emphasizes that existing studies are challenged by multimodal data, coupled degradation pathways, protocol dependence, sparse statistics, and uncertainty quantification, motivating AI-based analysis.
infographic.watch_item: Current AI approaches are limited by data quality, inconsistent protocols, weak benchmarks, interpretability gaps, and poor transferability across domains.
infographic.paper_title: Artificial Intelligence for Instability in Inorganic Perovskites: From Mechanism Discovery to Engineering Strategies

title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation
authors: Ana B. Cristóbal, Daniel Sierra, Laura Palomino, Luis Miguel Carrasco, Luis Narvarte
abstract: The success of distributed photovoltaics may be undermining its own future. As solar penetration increases, electricity prices decline during periods of peak generation, reducing the value of surplus photovoltaic production. This raises a critical question: can citizen-led energy systems remain economically viable in electricity markets dominated by renewable generation? Rather than exploring technically optimal but institutionally unrealistic solutions, we examine the options available under current regulatory and market conditions. Using high-resolution consumption data from a rural community sharing a PV facility among 24 users, we identify pathways for long-term sustainability. The study makes two contributions. First, it shows that effective internal coordination can mobilize participation and investment as successfully as external subsidies. Second, it compares static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing models, with and without storage, providing a flexible framework that balances efficiency, fairness, and governance. Results show that collective self-consumption reduces required PV capacity, lowers investment costs, and increases annual savings compared with individually operated systems. Alternative allocation schemes further improve benefit distribution and local electricity use, although gains depend on trade-offs between efficiency, fairness, and governance complexity. Under current electricity prices and remuneration schemes, battery storage provides limited additional economic value and becomes attractive only under specific market conditions. Overall, the long-term viability of citizen-led photovoltaic initiatives depends less on technological sophistication than on collective coordination and adaptive governance.

infographic.key_insight: Citizen-led PV remains viable under declining electricity prices mainly when users coordinate self-consumption and sharing strategies, not when relying on oversized generation or storage.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For distributed energy system design, the paper shows that governance and allocation rules can matter as much as hardware choices in maximizing local use, savings, and project sustainability.
method: Analyzed high-resolution consumption data from a rural community with 24 users sharing one PV facility
Compared static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing models
Evaluated configurations with and without battery storage under current market and remuneration conditions
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports that collective self-consumption lowers required PV capacity and investment cost while increasing annual savings versus individually operated systems, with storage adding limited value in most current-price scenarios.
infographic.watch_item: Benefits depend on trade-offs between efficiency, fairness, and governance complexity, so implementation may be harder than the technical optimization suggests.
infographic.paper_title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation

title: Dependence of charge separation efficiency on the exciton-charge transfer offset and Gaussian disorder in organic solar cells
authors: Maik Schwuchow, Carsten Deibel, Angela Thränhardt
abstract: State-of-the-art organic solar cells increasingly rely on low-offset semiconductor blends, challenging the traditional requirement of a large energetic driving force for efficient charge separation. In these systems, the energetic offset $ΔE_{\mathrm{LE-CT}}$ between local exciton (LE) and charge-transfer (CT) states approaches the thermal energy, making exciton-CT hybridization and thermal repopulation of the exciton level critical to device performance. In this work, we directly compare a macroscopic two-state rate model with three-dimensional kinetic Monte-Carlo (kMC) simulations to investigate microscopic charge separation dynamics and the role of Gaussian energetic disorder. We demonstrate that in the absence of disorder, the analytical rate model accurately reproduces kMC predictions for the whole range of $ΔE_{\mathrm{LE-CT}}$. Specifically, the macroscopic model successfully explains horizontal shifts in the internal quantum efficiency curves that arise depending on how the energetic offset is physically realized in the constituent molecules. We show that these variations can be captured entirely through the ratio of degeneracies of the LE and CT states, respectively. Introducing Gaussian energetic disorder into the kMC simulation reveals a distinct crossover behavior depending on $ΔE_{\mathrm{LE-CT}}$. While disorder is mostly detrimental at large offsets, it can significantly boost efficiency at intermediate and low offsets. Thermalization of charge carriers within the disorder-broadened density of states creates an effective driving force allowing charge separation even at zero or negative energetic offsets.

infographic.key_insight: Charge separation in low-offset organic solar cells is governed by the balance between LE–CT energetic offset, state degeneracy, and Gaussian disorder, which can either hinder or enhance efficiency depending on the regime.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Device design can improve performance by tuning molecular energetics and disorder so thermalization and exciton–CT hybridization sustain charge separation even at near-zero or negative offsets.
method: Compared a macroscopic two-state rate model against 3D kinetic Monte Carlo simulations.
Varied the LE–CT offset across the full range and mapped internal quantum efficiency trends.
Tested the impact of Gaussian energetic disorder on charge separation dynamics.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the analytical rate model matches kMC across all offsets without disorder, and that disorder changes the efficiency trend with a crossover from mostly harmful at large offsets to beneficial at intermediate and low offsets.
infographic.watch_item: The disorder-enhanced efficiency likely depends on material-specific energetic landscapes, so conclusions may not transfer directly without calibrating the offset and disorder parameters for a given blend.
infographic.paper_title: Dependence of charge separation efficiency on the exciton-charge transfer offset and Gaussian disorder in organic solar cells

title: First-principles calculations of spin-split bands in chiral hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$
authors: Tetsuya Furukawa, Kazushi Nakano, Youta Suzuki, Takumi Kaneko, Ayumi Ishii, Tetsuaki Itou
abstract: Chiral hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites provide a promising platform for investigating the physics of chirality-driven spin-split bands because they combine robust molecular chirality with strong spin-orbit coupling from heavy inorganic ions. First-principles calculations including spin-orbit coupling are performed for the one-dimensional chiral perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$ to compare their spin-split band structures and to identify the factors controlling their differences. In ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$, the lowest conduction bands predominantly consist of Pb orbitals, whereas in ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$, they are formed by hybridization between Pb orbitals and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital of NEA. Both compounds exhibit pronounced spin splitting near the valence-band maximum and conduction-band minimum. The effective spin splitting of the edges of the valence bands is stronger in ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$, despite similar linear-in-$k$ splitting coefficients near the relevant high-symmetry points. This enhancement originates from larger gaps induced by spin-orbit coupling at high-symmetry points and band (anti)crossings in the multiband structure. For a given molecular handedness, the PEA- and NEA-based compounds exhibit opposite spin textures, consistent with the opposite chiral distortions of the [PbI$_6$]$^{4-}$ octahedra and with the previously observed opposite signs of circular dichroism. Group-theoretical analysis for the nonsymmorphic space group $P2_12_12_1$ further accounts for band sticking, symmetry-enforced degeneracies, and the disappearance of spin polarization at specific Brillouin-zone-boundary points. These results provide a solid foundation for future studies of chirality-dependent electromagnetic responses, including circular dichroism, in chiral hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites.

infographic.key_insight: First-principles spin-orbit calculations show that chiral hybrid perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$ both host strong spin-split bands, but the magnitude and spin textures depend on molecular choice and chirality-driven octahedral distortions.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Understanding how ligand chirality and band hybridization tune spin splitting can guide the design of perovskite optoelectronic devices with controllable spin and circular-dichroic responses.
method: DFT calculations including spin-orbit coupling on one-dimensional chiral perovskites
Compare band structures, spin splitting, and spin textures for PEA- vs NEA-based compounds
Use group-theoretical analysis of space group $P2_12_12_1$ to explain degeneracies and band sticking
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports stronger valence-edge spin splitting in ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$ than in ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$, with opposite spin textures for opposite molecular handedness and symmetry-enforced features at Brillouin-zone boundaries.
infographic.watch_item: The results are theoretical and material-specific, so device-level performance and experimental stability still need validation.
infographic.paper_title: First-principles calculations of spin-split bands in chiral hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$

title: Photon Statistics from Yb3+-Doped CsPbCl3 are Inconsistent with Quantum Cutting
authors: Vincent R. M. Benning, Faris Horani, Daniel R. Gamelin, Freddy T. Rabouw
abstract: CsPb(Cl1-xBrx)3:Yb3+ has been widely reported as a broadband quantum-cutting material with a photoluminescence quantum yield exceeding 100%, making it a promising candidate for enhancing the blue-green spectral response of silicon photovoltaics. Many groups have reproduced absolute photoluminescence quantum yields over 100%, but others have struggled to obtain such high values. Here, we test the quantum-cutting capabilities of CsPbCl3:Yb3+ nanocrystals and bulk material using photon-correlation analysis. A quantum-cutting material is expected to exhibit photon bunching, but our experiments on CsPbCl3:Yb3+ show no such behavior. In fact, we observe the opposite -- anti-bunching -- under focused-excitation conditions. This observation can be explained with the previously established Auger-quenching pathway in CsPbCl3:Yb3+. Our results thus confirm high-power Auger quenching but question earlier descriptions of quantum cutting in CsPb(Cl1-xBrx)3:Yb3+.

infographic.key_insight: Photon-correlation measurements on Yb3+-doped CsPbCl3 do not support quantum cutting; instead, they show anti-bunching consistent with Auger quenching.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Claims of >100% photoluminescence quantum yield in Yb3+-doped lead-halide perovskites may not translate into reliable photon-multiplying performance for photovoltaic spectral conversion.
method: Performed photon-correlation analysis on CsPbCl3:Yb3+ nanocrystals and bulk samples.
Tested the expected photon bunching signature of quantum-cutting emission.
Compared observed emission statistics with the known Auger-quenching pathway.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports no photon bunching; instead, the measured emission under focused excitation shows anti-bunching, contradicting the quantum-cutting expectation.
infographic.watch_item: These results question the quantum-cutting interpretation in CsPb(Cl1-xBrx)3:Yb3+, so device designs should not assume >100% PLQY implies true photon doubling.
infographic.paper_title: Photon Statistics from Yb3+-Doped CsPbCl3 are Inconsistent with Quantum Cutting

title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
authors: Alexander Wieczorek, Manuel Kober-Czerny, Fábio Lopes, Austin George Kuba, Leon Müller, Christian M. Wolff
abstract: Accelerated ageing using elevated temperatures and illumination is one of the most common methods to rapidly study the stability of novel semiconductor materials. However, as the pace of materials discovery continues to accelerate, even faster stability evaluations are needed. A physics-informed time-series forecasting algorithm designed to predict the long-term photoluminescence stability of metal halide perovskites is presented. A diverse experimental dataset of 167 metal halide perovskites is collected, including different crystallinities and compositions. These are stressed using heat and light, while the photoluminescence (PL) is monitored. The >86k collected PL spectra are featurized using a physics-informed model, and a hybrid CNN-LSTM model is trained to forecast the PL intensity during degradation of samples unseen during model training. Notably, the approach generalizes across the material groups and outperforms baseline benchmarks. Furthermore, the physics-based featurization ensures explainability, enabling analysis to identify critical stability descriptors for given predictions. It is expected that this approach will be adapted to other types of time-series data and enables a pathway to significantly reduce experimental testing times.

infographic.key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term perovskite photoluminescence degradation from early-time spectra, enabling faster stability assessment of unseen materials.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This could substantially shorten accelerated aging campaigns for perovskite solar materials while providing interpretable stability descriptors for materials screening.
method: Collected 86k+ photoluminescence spectra from 167 metal halide perovskites under heat and light stress.
Converted spectra into physics-informed features to capture degradation behavior and improve explainability.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM model to predict future PL intensity for samples not seen during training.
infographic.evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on a diverse dataset spanning different crystallinities and compositions, and it outperformed baseline benchmarks while generalizing across material groups.
infographic.watch_item: Forecast quality may depend on how well the training data cover new perovskite chemistries, stress conditions, and measurement protocols.
infographic.paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability

title: Smart charging of large fleets of Electric Vehicles: Independent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approaches
authors: Xavier Rate, Eloann Le Guern, Raphaël Féraud, Fatma Salem, Melissa Chiknoun, Eymeric Giabicani
abstract: The electrification of transportation through electric vehicles introduces new challenges for power grid management, such as increased peak demand, voltage fluctuations, line overloads, and the integration of variable renewable energy sources. To enable efficient integration of EVs while minimizing costs for users and avoiding network overloads, implicit coordination between EVs is required. This work compares two independent multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches for optimizing such decentralized EV charging: contextual combinatorial bandits and policy gradient algorithms. Using a realistic simulation environment with autonomous agents making decisions based on local environmental information (including price signals, state-of-charge, and temporal constraints), we evaluate their performance across varying congestion levels, and mixed-strategy configurations with heterogeneous agent groups under dynamic electricity pricing derived from real photovoltaic production data.

infographic.key_insight: Independent multi-agent reinforcement learning can coordinate large EV fleets for smart charging without central control, helping reduce grid stress while respecting user constraints.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical framework for decentralized demand response that can limit peak demand, prevent overloads, and better align EV charging with variable electricity prices and renewable generation.
method: Compared contextual combinatorial bandits and policy gradient methods for decentralized EV charging control.
Agents used only local information such as price signals, state of charge, and time constraints.
Tested performance in a realistic simulation under different congestion levels and heterogeneous mixed-strategy fleet settings.
infographic.evidence_signal: The approaches were evaluated in simulation with dynamic electricity pricing derived from real photovoltaic production data across varying network congestion scenarios.
infographic.watch_item: Results depend on simulation assumptions and local-information policies, so real-world performance may vary under more complex grid constraints and user behavior.
infographic.paper_title: Smart charging of large fleets of Electric Vehicles: Independent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approaches

title: Boron-assisted stabilization of low-resistivity mixed-valence Cu-O thin films prepared by reactive magnetron sputtering
authors: Nirmal Kumar, Jemal Yimer Damte, Michal Procházka, Radomír Čerstvý, Jiří Houška, Pavel Baroch
abstract: This study systematically investigated the influence of boron incorporation in Cu-O thin films and the effect of oxygen partial pressure ($p_{\rm ox}$) on the phase evolution, chemical bonding, and electrical characteristics of the prepared films. A phase transition from Cu$_2$O to Cu$_2$O/Cu$_4$O$_3$ to CuO was observed as oxygen partial pressure increased. Boron incorporation significantly broadened the stability window of the Cu$_2$O and Cu$_4$O$_3$ phases and delayed the transition to CuO at higher oxygen partial pressure. In the highly B-doped Cu-O films, Cu$_4$O$_3$ was stabilized even under oxygen-rich conditions along with the CuO phase, suggesting that boron significantly altered the oxidation pathway. The formation of B-O and possible B-O-Cu configurations altered the local oxygen chemistry and promoted mixed-valence copper oxide phases. Electrical measurements revealed that highly B-doped Cu-O films exhibited a delayed transition from a high-resistivity low-$p_{\rm ox}$ regime to a low-resistivity mixed-valence regime, ultimately reaching approximately 0.06 $Ω$ cm, among the lowest reported resistivities for a CuO-like material. These findings demonstrate that boron doping is an effective approach for tailoring the phase stability, defect chemistry, and electrical characteristics of Cu-O thin films for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications.

infographic.key_insight: Boron doping expands the stable mixed-valence Cu-O phase window, delaying CuO formation and enabling much lower resistivity under oxygen-rich sputtering conditions.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This offers a controllable route to tune Cu-O thin-film conductivity and phase stability for transparent electrodes and photovoltaic/optoelectronic interfaces.
method: Reactive magnetron sputtering of Cu-O thin films with varying oxygen partial pressure.
Systematic boron incorporation to probe changes in phase evolution and bonding.
Characterization of phase, chemical bonding, and electrical resistivity across the processing window.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports a phase progression from Cu2O to Cu2O/Cu4O3 to CuO with increasing oxygen pressure, while highly B-doped films retained Cu4O3 under oxygen-rich conditions and reached about 0.06 Ω·cm.
infographic.watch_item: The reported benefits depend on precise oxygen partial pressure and boron incorporation control, so process reproducibility and phase purity may be challenging at scale.
infographic.paper_title: Boron-assisted stabilization of low-resistivity mixed-valence Cu-O thin films prepared by reactive magnetron sputtering

title: Fast and bright scintillators for ultrafast materials dynamics using 4th generation synchrotron
authors: Zhehui Wang, Dana Dattelbaum, Rachel Huber, Quanxi Jia, Yuelin Li, Katie Liu
abstract: We present recent advances in fast and bright scintillators for ultrafast X-ray phase contrast imaging of dynamic materials experiments at the upgraded Advanced Photon Source (APS-U), a fourth generation synchrotron. APS-U enables hard X-ray imaging at frame rates of at least 13 MHz (corresponding to 77 ns or shorter interframe intervals), creating a new need for scintillators with faster response and higher light output than lutetium yttrium oxyorthosilicate (LYSO). For indirect imaging and diffraction with ultrafast cameras, commercial lanthanum bromide (LaBr3) and cerium bromide (CeBr3) are promising candidates. These materials exhibit decay times approximately a factor of two shorter than LYSO (around 40 ns) and lutetium oxyorthosilicate (LSO), while maintaining comparable light yield per incident X-ray photon. However, their implementation at APS-U requires addressing several challenges, including material limitations due to hygroscopicity, efficient optical coupling to imaging systems, and high quantum efficiency for conversion of scintillation light, predominantly at wavelengths below 400 nm, into detectable electronic signals. We report results from material characterization, detector integration and packaging, and beamline experiments of materials with impact. In addition, emerging scintillator classes, including perovskites and high-entropy materials, are discussed as potential alternatives for next-generation ultrafast X-ray diagnostics.

infographic.key_insight: Fourth-generation synchrotron imaging needs scintillators that are both faster and brighter than LYSO, and LaBr3/CeBr3 are strong near-term candidates for ultrafast X-ray diagnostics.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Improving scintillator speed, light output, and UV-sensitive readout is critical for enabling 13 MHz hard X-ray phase-contrast imaging and dynamic materials experiments at APS-U.
method: Characterized fast scintillator materials for decay time and light yield
Integrated scintillators into detector/optical packaging for ultrafast cameras
Tested performance in beamline experiments and compared emerging alternatives
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports material characterization, detector integration, packaging, and beamline experiments showing LaBr3 and CeBr3 achieve about half the decay time of LYSO/LSO while maintaining comparable light yield.
infographic.watch_item: Many promising scintillators are hygroscopic and emit mainly below 400 nm, so packaging and high-quantum-efficiency UV readout remain major implementation challenges.
infographic.paper_title: Fast and bright scintillators for ultrafast materials dynamics using 4th generation synchrotron

title: Spin-Polarized Electronic Structure and Chemical Bonding Data for 2,500+ Halide Double Perovskites
authors: Luc Walterbos, Alex McEwan, Ravindra Shinde, Janine George, Linn Leppert
abstract: Halide double perovskites (A$_2$BB'X$_6$) are a long-known class of materials that has recently been rediscovered for diverse applications, including photovoltaics, photocatalysis, and radiation detection. Their doubled unit cell provides immense chemical tunability, allowing the incorporation of magnetic ions and enabling access to a wide range of electronic-structure features, including different band-edge characters, alignments, and symmetries. Magnetic elements may further introduce spin degrees of freedom and magnetic behaviour, thereby broadening the functional landscape of these compounds. Here, we present the first comprehensive database of spin-polarised electronic-structure data for all halide double perovskites predicted to be stable by the recently introduced $τ$ tolerance factor by Bartel et al. The dataset focuses on the Cs$_2$BB'X$_6$ family, with X = I, Br, Cl, and F, and includes density of states (DOS) for $>$2,500 compounds, calculated using hybrid-functional density functional theory. Among these, 719 compounds exhibit band gaps in the visible range and 118 display half-metallic character. In addition, we provide chemical-bonding analysis using \textsc{lobster}, which provides insights into orbital interactions across the dataset. To facilitate exploration, we further offer UMAP-based visualisations and an interactive app for systematic investigation of chemical composition, electronic structure, and magnetic properties.

infographic.key_insight: This study builds the first large spin-polarized electronic-structure database for stable halide double perovskites, revealing a rich pool of visible-gap and half-metallic candidates.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The dataset accelerates materials screening for photovoltaics, photocatalysis, and radiation detection by linking composition, band structure, magnetism, and bonding in one searchable resource.
method: Hybrid-functional DFT DOS calculations for >2,500 Cs2BB'X6 compounds (X = I, Br, Cl, F)
Stability screening based on the τ tolerance factor of Bartel et al.
LOBSTER bonding analysis plus UMAP visualizations and an interactive exploration app
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports more than 2,500 compounds, including 719 visible-band-gap materials and 118 half-metals, all supported by computed DOS and bonding descriptors.
infographic.watch_item: Results are computational and stability-filtered, so experimental validation is still needed before selecting specific candidates for device integration.
infographic.paper_title: Spin-Polarized Electronic Structure and Chemical Bonding Data for 2,500+ Halide Double Perovskites

title: Strongly frustrated 2D magnetism in a 3D hexagonal perovskite
authors: Bocheng Yu, Otkur Omar, Songtai Lv, Long Ma, Zhengcai Xia, Jing Meng
abstract: Exotic quantum phenomena are often found to occur in spin systems that exhibit low-dimensional magnetism. By combining nuclear magnetic resonance, neutron scattering, and muon-spin spectroscopy ($μ$SR) techniques, we report a rare instance of strongly frustrated two-dimensional (2D) magnetism in a three-dimensional (3D) hexagonal perovskite. Here, Ba$_2$La$_2$MnTe$_2$O$_{12}$, a triangular-lattice magnet, is shown to undergo a magnetic transition at $T_\mathrm{N} \approx$ 4.4 K, below which the manganese moments form a 120$^{\circ}$ AFM order within the $ab$-plane, while staying disordered along the $c$-axis. This exotic ground state, which exhibits ideal 2D magnetism, is highly consistent with the persistently strong spin fluctuations and the large internal field distributions revealed by zero-field $μ$SR. Further, the 2D magnetism also leads to a significant frustration, much larger than that of most known magnetically-ordered frustrated systems. Our work on Ba$_2$La$_2$MnTe$_2$O$_{12}$ not only challenges the interpretations of magnetic order in other 3D hexagonal perovskites, but it also provides insight into how the dimensionality affects the exotic magnetic states.

infographic.key_insight: Ba2La2MnTe2O12 shows unusually strong frustration and effectively ideal 2D antiferromagnetic order inside a 3D hexagonal perovskite, with 120° spins confined to the ab-plane and disordered along c.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This result highlights how lattice geometry and dimensionality can control emergent magnetic behavior, informing the design and interpretation of functional magnetic oxide materials.
method: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)
Neutron scattering
Muon-spin spectroscopy (μSR)
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports a magnetic transition at T_N ≈ 4.4 K and supporting μSR evidence of persistent spin fluctuations and broad internal field distributions.
infographic.watch_item: The conclusion of ideal 2D magnetism is based on low-temperature probe data in one compound, so broader material claims should be validated case by case.
infographic.paper_title: Strongly frustrated 2D magnetism in a 3D hexagonal perovskite

title: Electrical control of spin photocurrent in a magnetoelectric oxide Cr$_2$O$_3$
authors: Zhuo-Cheng Gu, Hiroaki Ishizuka
abstract: Controlling magnetism by electric field or current is a central topic in spintronics. In this work, we argue that the magnon spin photocurrent can also be controlled by the electric field in magnetoelectrics. Taking Cr$_2$O$_3$ as an example, we demonstrate how the spin current is modified by the electric field, using nonlinear response theory. We find that the Dzyaloshinsky--Moriya interaction induced by the applied field plays a key role in modifying spin-current conductivity, which exhibits pronounced anisotropy with respect to the light polarization. In particular, both the resonance frequency and the peak intensity show distinct dependences on the external electric field $E$, demonstrating electrical control of the spin photocurrent. In addition, we show that the two-magnon processes give rise to a continuum spectrum, a consequence of the field-induced spin canting. These results show that Cr$_2$O$_3$ is a promising platform for realizing electrically tunable spin photovoltaic effect.

infographic.key_insight: An applied electric field can tune magnon-mediated spin photocurrent in Cr2O3 by modifying the Dzyaloshinsky–Moriya interaction and thus the spin-current conductivity.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This suggests a route to electrically controllable spin photovoltaic devices, where polarization-dependent photocurrent can be actively tuned in magnetoelectric oxides.
method: Used nonlinear response theory to model magnon spin photocurrent in Cr2O3.
Analyzed how an external electric field induces Dzyaloshinsky–Moriya interaction and spin canting.
Compared resonance frequency, peak intensity, and polarization anisotropy under varying electric field.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports field-dependent shifts in resonance frequency and peak intensity, plus a two-magnon continuum spectrum from field-induced spin canting.
infographic.watch_item: The results are theoretical for a specific magnetoelectric oxide, so experimental validation and material/device integration may be challenging.
infographic.paper_title: Electrical control of spin photocurrent in a magnetoelectric oxide Cr$_2$O$_3$

title: A green solvent screening tool for emerging materials via uncertainty aware, transformer enhanced transfer learning
authors: Ioannis Kouroudis, Simon Ternes, Zhaosu Gu, Gohar Ali Siddiqui, Marina Ustinova, Angelo Lembo
abstract: Accurate prediction of solubility remains a central challenge across materials science and sustainable chemistry. In particular due to emerging technologies like organic and hybrid photovoltaics, batteries, and catalysis, solvent usage is expected to increase significantly within the coming years. Therefore, substituting solvents with greener alternatives is vital. This is where machine learning can have substantial impact. However, the limited data on critical parameters of solubility significantly constraints machine learning efficacy. In this work, we transfer a pre-trained foundational model on QM9 targets to our application with minimal data requirements. Additionally, the pipeline integrates uncertainty quantification, allowing the user to gauge the confidence of the predictions. As baseline, we succeed in predicting the Hansen solubility parameters and Dielectric Constant for which extensive databases exist. Importantly, we achieve high model performance on additional targets, such as Gutmann Donor and Acceptor numbers, where the available data is extremely limited. Overall, we augment data on solubility descriptors by orders of magnitude with high quality predictions. For effective dissemination, we deploy easy-to-use, easily integrateable with high throughput labs, customizable tool for ranking and screening possible solvent substitutes. Finally, we rediscovered known green solvent alternatives and proposed new candidates proving its relevance for finding eco-friendly solvents.

infographic.key_insight: A transfer-learned, uncertainty-aware transformer can screen greener solvent substitutes for emerging materials even when solubility data are sparse.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The tool helps high-throughput materials workflows replace harmful solvents by ranking candidates with practical confidence estimates for photovoltaic and related chemistry applications.
method: Pre-train on QM9 targets, then transfer to solubility-related properties with minimal labeled data.
Add uncertainty quantification so users can assess prediction confidence during screening.
Deploy an easy-to-integrate ranking pipeline for solvent substitution and candidate discovery.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong performance on well-studied solubility descriptors and on harder, data-scarce targets such as Gutmann donor and acceptor numbers, while also recovering known green solvents and suggesting new ones.
infographic.watch_item: Predictions are only as reliable as the domain transfer and uncertainty calibration, so sparse or out-of-domain chemistries may still need experimental validation.
infographic.paper_title: A green solvent screening tool for emerging materials via uncertainty aware, transformer enhanced transfer learning

title: Accelerated development of amorphous InZnO thin films as transparent conductive Cu diffusion barriers
authors: Stefanie Frick, Reyu Sakakibara, Manuel Kober-Czerny, Arnold Müller, Miloš Baljozović, Franz-Josef Haug
abstract: In light of the increasing supply chain concerns regarding silver for solar cell metallization, the replacement of the silver contacts by copper is desirable. As copper diffuses readily in silicon, deposition of an additional diffusion barrier to protect the respective absorber material stacks is required. We investigate multifunctional layers of transparent conductive oxides (TCOs) from the In-Zn-O system to serve as front electrode and Cu diffusion barrier coating, focusing on purely amorphous layers without grain boundaries to impede copper diffusion. We employ a 2D combinatorial approach to simultaneously screen the Zn/(In+Zn) ratio and the oxygen content in a single materials library deposited by magnetron sputtering without intentional substrate heating. Cu diffusion barrier performance was evaluated by depositing Cu on top of intentionally ultrathin In-Zn-O libraries of 7 nm on silicon wafers and annealing them at temperatures of 200-450°C. Both the formation of copper silicides, as well as the silicon photoluminescence signal were monitored. The first was detected only after the crystallization of the In-Zn-O films and required annealing temperatures of 450°C and above. Even for extended dwell times of 20 h at a relevant process temperature of 200°C, we find no evidence of Cu ingress for most of our fabricated In-Zn-O compositions, whereas Si/Cu stacks without In-Zn-O barriers showed a reduction of their photo-luminescence intensity already after less than 1 h. These results suggest thin amorphous In-Zn-O films with an optimal Zn/(In+Zn) ratio of ~0.12 and intermediate oxygen deficiency as effective transparent conductive Cu diffusion barriers for solar cell applications.

infographic.key_insight: Purely amorphous In-Zn-O thin films can act as both transparent conductive layers and effective Cu diffusion barriers, with best performance near Zn/(In+Zn) ≈ 0.12 and intermediate oxygen deficiency.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable route to replace silver metallization with copper in solar cells while protecting silicon absorbers from Cu contamination.
method: 2D combinatorial sputtering screened Zn/(In+Zn) ratio and oxygen content in one materials library
7 nm ultrathin In-Zn-O films were deposited on Si without intentional substrate heating
Cu-overlayer stacks were annealed at 200–450°C and assessed via copper silicide formation plus Si photoluminescence
infographic.evidence_signal: Cu ingress was not detected for most In-Zn-O compositions even after 20 h at 200°C, while unprotected Si/Cu stacks lost photoluminescence in under 1 h; Cu silicides appeared only after crystallization at 450°C and above.
infographic.watch_item: Barrier performance depends on maintaining the film amorphous state, so thermal crystallization during processing could weaken protection.
infographic.paper_title: Accelerated development of amorphous InZnO thin films as transparent conductive Cu diffusion barriers

title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
authors: Jubair Hossan Abir, Tauhidur Rahman, S. S. B. Pallab, Md. Sharear Aman, R. S. Islam, S. H. Naqib
abstract: In this study, the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties of the novel lead-free halide double perovskite series beta2SnGeX6 (beta = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) are systematically investigated using density functional theory (DFT). Calculated formation energies, Tolerance factors, and octahedral factors confirm that all six compounds exhibit robust thermodynamic stability within a highly symmetric cubic geometry. Mechanical analysis derived from elastic parameters characterizes the entire series as fundamentally ductile, ensuring high processing elasticity and resistance to micro-cracking during device manufacturing. Electronic band structures reveal direct bandgaps showing exceptional composition-dependent tunability from 1.44 eV down to 0.64 eV via progressive halogen substitution. The wide gap chloride variations are optimized for single-junction photovoltaic absorbers, while the narrower-gap bromide and iodide analogs show immense promise for tandem solar architectures and near-infrared photodetectors. Thermoelectrically, heavy constituent atoms introduce strong lattice anharmonicity and intense high-temperature Umklapp phonon scattering, significantly suppressing lattice thermal conductivity. Combined with low carrier effective masses that optimize electrical transport, the iodide compounds achieve higher power factors and outstanding dimensionless figures of merit (ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K). Ultimately, these lead-free double perovskite family emerges as an environmentally benign and versatile platform for next-generation green optoelectronics and solid-state waste-heat recovery.

infographic.key_insight: DFT predicts that lead-free double perovskites K/Rb2SnGeX6 are stable, mechanically ductile, and electronically tunable across a wide direct-bandgap range by halogen substitution.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These materials could be tailored for photovoltaic absorbers, tandem solar cells, photodetectors, and high-performance thermoelectric waste-heat recovery without relying on toxic lead.
method: Density functional theory calculations of structure, electronic bands, optics, mechanics, and thermoelectrics
Stability screening using formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor
Property comparison across X = Cl, Br, I and beta = K, Rb compositions
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust cubic stability, direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 eV to 0.64 eV, and a peak thermoelectric performance of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
infographic.watch_item: The conclusions are computational and need experimental synthesis, defect, and long-term device stability validation before application.
infographic.paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications

title: Machine-learned dynamics of surface polarons at reduced oxide surfaces
authors: Luca Leoni, Cesare Franchini
abstract: Reducible oxides exhibit a rich interplay of electronic, structural, and chemical properties that underpins applications in catalysis, photovoltaics, batteries, and energy storage. This interplay is strongly shaped by excess electrons, often introduced by oxygen vacancies, that localize as small polarons and influence charge transport and surface chemistry. At surfaces, these polarons play a central role in charge localization, mobility, and reactivity, yet their finite-temperature dynamics remain difficult to access from first principles. Ab initio molecular dynamics is typically limited to picosecond time scales, precluding statistically meaningful sampling of polaron hopping dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we extend machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics [V. Birschitzky et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 216301 (2025)] to redox-active oxide surfaces, using oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110) as a paradigmatic case. By accessing several nanoseconds of dynamics over a range of temperatures, we show that small-polaron mobility at the reduced rutile TiO2(110) surface is suppressed by several orders of magnitude relative to the corresponding bulk material, providing a microscopic interpretation of the lower electron mobilities observed in porous rutile TiO2 compared with single-crystal samples. This suppressed mobility arises from the loss of favorable hopping pathways: surface polaron motion is largely confined to planar inter-row trajectories within the second topmost layers, with only rare interlayer hopping events. Oxygen vacancies further reshape the polaron free-energy landscape by acting as attractive centers for excess electrons, biasing the polaron distribution toward nearby Ti sites and promoting occasional charge transfer to the outermost surface layer. These results establish a transferable machine-learning strategy for investigating polaron dynamics in reducible oxides.

infographic.key_insight: Machine-learned simulations show that small polarons at reduced rutile TiO2(110) surfaces move far more slowly than in the bulk because surface geometry removes efficient hopping pathways.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This helps explain the low electron mobility in porous rutile TiO2 and informs the design of oxide surfaces for catalysis, photovoltaics, batteries, and energy storage.
method: Extended machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics to a redox-active oxide surface
Ran several nanoseconds of finite-temperature dynamics on oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110)
Analyzed polaron hopping pathways, layer-resolved mobility, and vacancy-induced free-energy changes
infographic.evidence_signal: The study uses nanosecond-scale simulations across a temperature range and reports several-orders-of-magnitude lower surface mobility than in the corresponding bulk material.
infographic.watch_item: The conclusions depend on the accuracy and transferability of the machine-learned model for capturing rare hopping events and vacancy effects on complex surfaces.
infographic.paper_title: Machine-learned dynamics of surface polarons at reduced oxide surfaces

title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
authors: Jiban Kangsabanik, Kasper Tolborg, Thomas Olsen, Kristian S. Thygesen
abstract: Understanding how point defects fundamentally influence photovoltaic performance remains a central question for emerging wide-band gap absorbers. Trigonal selenium (t-Se) has recently re-emerged as a promising photovoltaic material due to its near-optimal band gap for tandem and indoor applications. Here we quantify defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination in t-Se using first principles calculations across a large and chemically diverse set of point defects. Our results suggest that t-Se is intrinsically defect tolerant. Despite the presence of multiple deep levels in the gap, recombination via nonradiative multi-phonon emission processes is strongly suppressed by large lattice reorganizations and large energy releases of at least 0.5 EG per recombination event, while radiative defect-assisted capture also remains too small to account for the observed device losses. Consequently, SRH recombination mediated by realistic concentrations of point defects cannot account for the observed efficiency limitations in selenium photovoltaics. We explore trends in both radiative and nonradiative SRH recombination rates across the defect data set, highlighting their complex dependence on defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions. These findings establish trigonal selenium as a defect-tolerant wide-band-gap absorber and provide transferable design principles for optimizing next-generation photovoltaic materials for tandem and indoor applications.

infographic.key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though many point defects create deep gap states, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed performance losses.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, with defect engineering likely less critical than in many other emerging PV materials.
method: First-principles calculations on a large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium
Computed Shockley-Read-Hall recombination pathways, including nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture
Compared recombination trends versus defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions
infographic.evidence_signal: Across the defect dataset, recombination is strongly suppressed by large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 E_G per event, and realistic defect concentrations still cannot explain the measured efficiency limits.
infographic.watch_item: The conclusions are based on defect-limited recombination modeling, so device losses from interfaces, contacts, morphology, or extended defects may still be important in real cells.
infographic.paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
